judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The image is a tile of the client-rendered StoryStream #LoveMatalan gallery: an img that is not inside a control (the tile's separate button is named "Read more about ...'s instagram-user post"), with the template alt "Instagram post by shopmatalan" that every tile by that account shares. claimTrue: no as worded; the alt is accurate about provenance (the tile's author line and Instagram icon agree), so it does not describe something absent, it omits what the picture shows. elementFails: yes. The picture is informative (it is the post's look, the gallery's point), and the alt neither describes it nor gives the scene (a woman in a black blazer outfit by a Christmas tree). The skeptic reasons checked do not hold up: the image is not a control whose alt only needs to name a function; the tile's caption is the post's truncated text, not a description of the picture; the tile is a video post, but this img is a separate still poster, and even the time-based-media exception would need descriptive identification, which an alt shared by every post of the account is not. Read in good faith, the claim names this failure (the rubric's own example of this wording), so true_positive. captureDiffers: cannot_tell. The live server HTML holds only the empty widget mount (#stry-wrapper), so my fetch cannot render the gallery to compare; the capture is a styled real-browser render and nothing suggests users received other alts.
